definition: In diagnosis, an interval of uncertainty is a range of test decision thresholds where the result is not clear enough to support a confident classification. It can be identified alongside ROC-based methods to improve prediction by marking values that are diagnostically uncertain.

reasons: The packet does not define the term as a range of test decision thresholds where the result is not clear enough to support a confident classification; it only says the interval of uncertainty was used to identify thresholds of uncertainty and enhance prediction.

The added claim that it is identified alongside ROC-based methods to improve prediction is only partially supported and is stated too generally; the source mentions two-graph ROC in a specific study, not a general definitional relationship for the term.
The packet does not provide a definition of “interval of uncertainty”; it only mentions “thresholds of uncertainty … and the interval of uncertainty” in the context of enhancing prediction.
The definition’s claims about “a range of test decision thresholds” and “not clear enough to support a confident classification” are not stated or supported in the supplied packet.

The definition’s attribution to being “identified alongside ROC-based methods” is only partially supported: the packet mentions ROC/“two-graph ROC” thresholds of uncertainty, but does not describe this as “diagnostically uncertain” or as an identifiable “range” for diagnosis.

The packet does not support the wording that the interval is “used … to improve prediction by marking values that are diagnostically uncertain.” It only indicates it was used “to enhance prediction” and mentions uncertainty thresholds, without the described diagnostic-certainty rationale.
